$meta.description: Composition rules for Construct CLI screens. Machine-readable lint spec — Claude validates new screens against these rules, and generates matching rules when creating new patterns.

glyph_color_pairs.$description: Each glyph has a fixed set of valid colors. Using a glyph with any other color is an error.

glyph_usage.$description: Each glyph has specific contexts where it's allowed. Using it elsewhere is a warning.
glyph_usage.●: Major section headers (error sections, action headers during progress). Never decorative.
glyph_usage.▶: Recovery actions, next-step entries, empty-state recovery. Always leads a concrete runnable command.
glyph_usage.✓: Sub-task completion summaries. Always past-tense count + noun (e.g. '42 repositories modified').
glyph_usage.⚠: Non-fatal warning count lines. Always leads with a count, cause in parentheses.
glyph_usage.?: Inline hints. Always followed by 'Hint:' as leading word.
glyph_usage.!: Inline notes or errors. Leading word determines color: 'Note:' = warning, 'Error:' = danger.
glyph_usage.└: Sub-description under numbered onboarding steps only.
glyph_usage.$: Shell prompt in EXAMPLES blocks only.

color_usage.$description: Semantic colors have specific contexts. Using them outside these contexts is a warning.
semantic.danger: error section headers (● WHAT WENT WRONG, ● TRY)
semantic.warning: PARTIAL SUCCESS preface and close banner
text.metadata: structural framing (─ rules in start banner)

section_headers.$description: Section headers are ALL CAPS, bold, followed immediately by content (0 blank lines).

close_banners.$description: Every command exit produces exactly one close banner — or none for help screens, inline errors, and progress-in-flight.

rules.rule: Glyph-color pairing is invariant
rules.description: Every glyph must use one of its valid colors from glyph_color_pairs. No exceptions.

rules.rule: No bare glyphs without semantic purpose
rules.description: A glyph must always carry meaning. ● marks a major section, ▶ leads a command, ✓ reports a result. Decorative use is not allowed.

rules.rule: ▶ always leads a concrete, runnable command
rules.description: The text after ▶ must be something you can paste into a terminal. No exploratory suggestions or prose.

rules.rule: Section headers are ALL CAPS
rules.description: Section headers use typography.section_header — bold, ALL CAPS, letter-spaced. Mixed case is not a header.

rules.rule: Prefer existing section headers before inventing new ones
rules.description: Check section_headers.known_headers first. New headers are allowed but should be flagged for review.

rules.rule: Exactly 1 blank line between sections
rules.description: No double-blanks, no zero-blanks between sections. Header-to-content is 0 blanks.

rules.rule: Section content indented 2 spaces
rules.description: Body lines under a section header indent 2 spaces. Continuation lines (under ▶, examples) indent 4 spaces.

rules.rule: No more than 3 semantic colors per screen
rules.description: A single CLI screen should use at most 3 of the 4 semantic colors (danger, success, warning, info). Using all 4 signals unclear intent.

rules.rule: Danger (red) only for failure states
rules.description: Red is reserved for: error sections, failure banners, error markers, failure row glyphs. Never for emphasis or attention.

rules.rule: Info (cyan) only for actionable content
rules.description: Cyan is for things you can run, click, or navigate to: commands, flags, paths, URLs. Not for labels or descriptions.

rules.rule: Close banner matches exit condition
rules.description: Success → green MOD SUCCEEDED. Failure → red MOD FAILED. Partial → yellow MOD PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED. No mismatches.

rules.rule: Close banner is the last visible content
rules.description: Nothing renders after the close banner. It's the final line of the screen.

rules.rule: Help screens and inline errors have no close banner
rules.description: Help is informational. Inline errors never started execution. Neither produces a banner.

rules.rule: Full error follows five-element shape
rules.description: FAILURE preface → WHAT WENT WRONG (one-line body) → optional ? Hint → TRY (recovery actions) → MOD FAILED banner.

rules.rule: WHAT WENT WRONG body is exactly one line
rules.description: Names the concrete input that failed. Multi-cause explanation goes in the ? Hint block, not the body.

rules.rule: TRY lists recovery actions in likelihood order
rules.description: Most-likely-to-help first. Support line (support@) is always last, demoted to metadata when other suggestions precede.

rules.rule: Success screens need at least one ✓ result row
rules.description: A success screen without a concrete result (what was done, how many) is incomplete.

rules.rule: Leaf help starts with summary + consequence prose
rules.description: First line: what the command does. Next 1-3 lines: what happens if you don't do it, or what it enables.

rules.rule: EXAMPLES use real values, USAGE uses placeholders
rules.description: USAGE shows the syntax with <placeholders>. EXAMPLES show concrete invocations with real paths and flags.

rules.rule: Tables with 3+ rows should have a trailing summary
rules.description: Restate the count and per-status breakdown in one line below the table.

rules.rule: Empty state uses 'No <noun-phrase>.' format
rules.description: Sentence case, period, no glyph. Supporting color. Optional ▶ recovery action below.

rules.rule: Step numbering is continuous across groups
rules.description: Numbers never restart at each group header. Carries the 'do these in order' semantic.

rules.rule: Each step is exactly one command + one └ description
rules.description: No third line. Command in cyan, └ description in supporting. Step number in green.

rules.rule: Action headers use gerund verb, no period
rules.description: 'Running recipe on 47 repositories' not 'Run recipe' or 'Running recipe on 47 repositories.'

rules.rule: Inline command references are cyan, not bold
rules.description: Bold is reserved for section headers and banner phrases. Commands in prose are regular weight, cyan only.

rules.rule: New patterns must ship with composition rules
rules.description: When generating a screen that doesn't match an existing pattern, also generate a draft pattern spec with required/optional sections and constraints. Flag for review.

rules.rule: Check existing patterns before creating new ones
rules.description: Search the 11 canonical patterns for a match before composing a novel screen. Most new screens are variations of existing patterns.

pattern_shapes.$description: Required and optional elements for each pattern type. Used for lint validation and as generation templates.

optional: WHAT TO DO NEXT (▶ entries with em-dash gloss)

inline-command-reference.note: Not a standalone screen — a text-level treatment used inside other patterns.
